question:
An engineer must implement an automation solution to allow the backup of the configuration of Cisco Nexus Series Switches to a centralized location. The solution must:
* support the team-developed custom monitoring scripts that are packaged using RPM packaging that the framework must support.
* be decoupled from the underlying Cisco Nexus operating system.
* have no impact on the operating system of the underlying switch if resource contention occurs.
* use Python to expand the existing automation framework.
Which solution meets these requirements?
theory: Guest Shell is a decoupled, resource-limited Linux Container (CPU/memory/rootfs caps independently configurable) so a custom monitoring application can't starve the host NX-OS process even under contention, and it ships Python plus pip/YUM, letting you install team-built RPM-packaged tools directly. Bash shell runs closer to the host with less isolation, and 'Vegas Shell'/'TCL Shell' aren't real decoupled execution environments on NX-OS, so Guest Shell uniquely satisfies all four stated requirements. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
